newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani road tankers call off strike.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani road tankers call off strike.

text.p: Pakistan's private transporters of edible oils and petroleum products called off their 30-day-old strike on Tuesday and will resume operations immediately, a spokesman for them said.
"The strike has been called off after authorities agreed to fulfil our demands," the spokesman for the Oil Tanker (truck) Owners Association said.

He said the authorities had agreed to raise the transporters' cartage fee while the association agreed to follow a queue system to lift vegetable oils from the Karachi port instead of a contract system.
The strike had cut edible oil supplies to processing mills, leading to higher prices in the local markets.
The shortage of petroleum products was not so severe as most petroleum distribution companies were able to feed petrol filling stations with their own fleet of tankers.
The association had first called off the strike on Friday, but a dispute over the fee increase took the tanker trucks off the roads again on Sunday.
